goal: Check in for a flight and hand over your luggage at the counter.

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Hi, I'd like to check in for the 4pm flight to Dubai.

conversation.speaker: Agent
conversation.text: Of course. May I see your passport, please?

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Here you are. I have one bag to check.

conversation.speaker: Agent
conversation.text: Please place it on the belt. Would you prefer a window or an aisle seat?

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: An aisle seat, please. And which gate is it?

conversation.speaker: Agent
conversation.text: Gate 32. Boarding starts at 3:20.

keyExpressions: I'd like to check in for the flight to…
I have one bag to check.
remember: Staff will ask if you packed your bags yourself. It is a routine security question — a simple 'yes' is the expected answer.

goal: Arrive at a hotel where you already have a booking and get to your room.

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Good evening. I have a reservation under the name Menon.

conversation.speaker: Receptionist
conversation.text: Let me check… yes, a double room for three nights. May I see your passport?

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Here you go. What time is breakfast served?

conversation.speaker: Receptionist
conversation.text: From seven to ten in the restaurant on the ground floor.

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Perfect. And what time is check-out?

conversation.speaker: Receptionist
conversation.text: Eleven, but we can hold your bags afterwards if you need.

keyExpressions: Could I have a late check-out?
remember: 'Under the name…' is the standard phrasing for any booking — hotels, restaurants, and appointments alike.

goal: Order a meal and ask for the bill in a casual restaurant.

conversation.speaker: Waiter
conversation.text: Good evening. Are you ready to order?

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Almost — could I have another minute with the menu?

conversation.speaker: Waiter
conversation.text: Take your time. Today's special is grilled fish.

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: That sounds good. I'll have the fish, please. Does it come with rice?

conversation.speaker: Waiter
conversation.text: It comes with potatoes, but I can change it to rice.

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Rice would be great, thank you.

keyExpressions: Could we get the bill, please?
remember: 'I'll have…' is the natural way to order. 'I want…' is grammatically fine but sounds abrupt to English ears.

goal: Find your way when you are lost in an unfamiliar place.

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Excuse me, could you tell me how to get to the station?

conversation.speaker: Passer-by
conversation.text: Sure. Go straight down this road and turn left at the traffic lights.

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Straight, then left at the lights. Is it far?

conversation.speaker: Passer-by
conversation.text: About ten minutes on foot.

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Thank you so much.

keyExpressions: Excuse me, could you tell me how to get to…?
Am I going the right way for…?
Sorry, could you say that again more slowly?
Is there a bus that goes there?
remember: Always start with 'Excuse me'. Approaching a stranger without it sounds abrupt in English.
Repeating the directions back confirms you understood and gives the other person a chance to correct you.

term: The Start of a Job Interview
goal: Handle the opening minutes of an interview, including 'tell me about yourself'.

conversation.speaker: Interviewer
conversation.text: Thanks for coming in. Would you like some water before we start?

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: I'm fine, thank you. It's good to be here.

conversation.speaker: Interviewer
conversation.text: Let's begin — tell me a little about yourself.

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Of course. I've worked in customer support for four years, most recently leading a small team. I'm looking for a role with more responsibility for process design, which is why this position interested me.

conversation.speaker: Interviewer
conversation.text: And what do you know about our company?

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: I read about your expansion into the Gulf market last year, and I'd be keen to hear how that's changed the support side.

keyExpressions: I'm looking for a role where I can…
That's why this position interested me.
I'd be keen to hear more about…
remember: 'Tell me about yourself' is asking about your professional story, not your personal life. Two minutes is enough.
Ending an answer with a question of your own turns the interview into a conversation.

goal: Describe a symptom clearly and understand the advice you are given.

conversation.speaker: Doctor
conversation.text: What seems to be the problem?

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: I've had a sore throat for about a week, and now a cough.

conversation.speaker: Doctor
conversation.text: Any fever?

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: A slight one, mostly in the evenings.

conversation.speaker: Doctor
conversation.text: I'll take a look. It's likely viral, so rest and fluids should be enough.

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Should I come back if it doesn't improve?

keyExpressions: I've had… for about a week.
Should I come back if it doesn't improve?
How often should I take this?
remember: 'I've had it for a week' uses the present perfect because the problem is still happening — this is the natural tense for symptoms.

goal: Return or exchange an item you have already bought.

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Hi, I'd like to return this — it doesn't fit.

conversation.speaker: Assistant
conversation.text: No problem. Do you have the receipt?

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Yes, here it is. Can I get a refund?

conversation.speaker: Assistant
conversation.text: I can refund it to the original card. It takes three to five working days.

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: That's fine, thank you.

keyExpressions: Could I exchange it for a different size?
Do you have this in a larger size?
remember: 'Return' means give it back; 'exchange' means swap it for something else. Shops treat these as different requests.

goal: Answer a work call professionally and take a message.

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Good morning, Anish speaking.

conversation.speaker: Caller
conversation.text: Hi, is Meera available?

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: She's in a meeting at the moment. Can I take a message?

conversation.speaker: Caller
conversation.text: Please — could you ask her to call me back about the invoice?

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Of course. Could I take your name and number?

conversation.speaker: Caller
conversation.text: It's Daniel Cruz, 07700 900123.

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Got it. I'll pass that on as soon as she's free.

keyExpressions: Could I take your name and number?
Could you spell that for me?
remember: Reading a number or a name back to the caller is standard practice and prevents most message errors.

goal: Open an account or sort out a problem at a bank counter.

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Hello, I'd like to open a current account.

conversation.speaker: Clerk
conversation.text: Certainly. Do you have proof of address and ID with you?

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: I have my passport and a utility bill. Will that do?

conversation.speaker: Clerk
conversation.text: That's perfect. Are there any monthly fees you'd like me to explain?

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Yes, please — and is there a minimum balance?

keyExpressions: I'd like to open an account.
Do you need proof of address?
How long does the transfer take?
remember: 'Will that do?' is a natural, slightly informal way to ask whether something is acceptable.

goal: Ask the right questions when viewing a place to live.

conversation.speaker: Agent
conversation.text: This is the living room, and the kitchen is through there.

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: It's bigger than it looked online. Are bills included in the rent?

conversation.speaker: Agent
conversation.text: Water is included, but not electricity or internet.

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: And how much is the deposit?

conversation.speaker: Agent
conversation.text: Five weeks' rent, returned at the end of the tenancy.

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Understood. When would it be available from?

keyExpressions: Is there a minimum contract length?
remember: Ask specifically which bills are included. 'Bills included' rarely means all of them.

goal: Complain about poor service in a way that gets the problem fixed.

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Excuse me — I'm sorry to bother you, but there's a problem with our order.

conversation.speaker: Manager
conversation.text: I'm sorry to hear that. What's happened?

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: We ordered forty minutes ago and the table next to us was served first.

conversation.speaker: Manager
conversation.text: That shouldn't have happened. Let me check the kitchen right away.

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Thank you. We're happy to wait, we'd just like to know how long.

keyExpressions: I'm sorry to bother you, but…
There seems to be a problem with…
I'd just like to know how long.
remember: Describing the facts calmly works far better than expressing anger. 'There seems to be a problem' invites help rather than defensiveness.

term: Meeting a Client for the First Time
goal: Greet a new client and open a business conversation.

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Ms Okafor? I'm Anish, we spoke on email. Very nice to meet you at last.

conversation.speaker: Client
conversation.text: Likewise. Please call me Ada.

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Thanks, Ada. Did you find us all right?

conversation.speaker: Client
conversation.text: Easily, thanks. The directions were clear.

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Good. Shall we go through to the meeting room? Can I get you a coffee on the way?

keyExpressions: Nice to meet you at last.
Did you find us all right?
remember: Start formally with a surname and let the other person invite you to use their first name. Following their lead is always safe.

goal: Buy a train or bus ticket and confirm the details.

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Hello, one ticket to Manchester, please.

conversation.speaker: Clerk
conversation.text: Single or return?

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Return, coming back on Sunday.

conversation.speaker: Clerk
conversation.text: That's forty-two pounds. Platform four, leaving at 10:15.

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Do I need to change trains?

conversation.speaker: Clerk
conversation.text: No, it's direct.

keyExpressions: What time does the next one leave?
remember: British English says 'single' and 'return'; American English says 'one-way' and 'round-trip'.

goal: Fill a short wait with easy conversation.

conversation.speaker: Colleague
conversation.text: Morning! Did you have a good weekend?

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Not bad, thanks — mostly quiet. How about you?

conversation.speaker: Colleague
conversation.text: We went walking on Sunday. Beautiful weather.

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: It really was. Where did you go?

conversation.speaker: Colleague
conversation.text: Up near the reservoir. Have you been?

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Not yet, but it's on my list.

keyExpressions: Did you have a good weekend?
Not bad, thanks — how about you?
remember: Always return the question. Small talk dies immediately if only one person is asking.

goal: Ask for medicine and understand how to take it.

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Hi, do you have anything for a blocked nose?

conversation.speaker: Pharmacist
conversation.text: Is it for you? Any other symptoms?

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Just me, and a mild headache.

conversation.speaker: Pharmacist
conversation.text: This spray should help. Twice a day, no more than five days.

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Can I take it with paracetamol?

conversation.speaker: Pharmacist
conversation.text: Yes, that's fine.

keyExpressions: How often should I take it?
Is it available without a prescription?
remember: 'Do you have anything for…?' is the standard opening — you describe the symptom, not the medicine.

goal: Chase a missing order over the phone.

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Hi, I'm calling about an order that was due on Tuesday and hasn't arrived.

conversation.speaker: Agent
conversation.text: Sorry about that. Do you have the order number?

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Yes — it's 4471-B.

conversation.speaker: Agent
conversation.text: I can see it's still at the depot. I'll arrange redelivery for Friday.

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Friday doesn't work for me. Could it come on Saturday instead?

conversation.speaker: Agent
conversation.text: Let me see what I can do.

keyExpressions: I'm calling about an order that hasn't arrived.
Do you have the order number? — Yes, it's…
remember: 'That doesn't work for me' is a firm but polite refusal — much better than 'no' when you need a different option.

goal: Ask about membership options before signing up.

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Hi, I'd like to know about your membership options.

conversation.speaker: Staff
conversation.text: Sure. We have monthly and annual plans. The annual one works out cheaper.

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Is there a joining fee?

conversation.speaker: Staff
conversation.text: Twenty pounds, but it's waived this month.

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: And can I cancel the monthly plan any time?

conversation.speaker: Staff
conversation.text: Yes, with a month's notice.

remember: 'Works out cheaper' means cheaper once you calculate the total — a very common everyday phrasing.

goal: Introduce two people who have not met.

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Ravi, this is Elena — she runs the design team.

conversation.speaker: Ravi
conversation.text: Nice to meet you, Elena.

conversation.speaker: Elena
conversation.text: You too. How do you two know each other?

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: We worked together at my last company.

conversation.speaker: Elena
conversation.text: Ah, so you've heard all the stories.

keyExpressions: Nice to meet you. — You too.
How do you two know each other?
I've heard a lot about you.
remember: Add one detail about each person. It gives them something to talk about after you walk away.

term: Asking Your Manager for Time Off
goal: Request leave and address the impact on your work.

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Do you have a minute? I wanted to ask about taking some leave.

conversation.speaker: Manager
conversation.text: Of course. When were you thinking?

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: The last week of March, if that works. I've checked and nothing major is due then.

conversation.speaker: Manager
conversation.text: That should be fine. Can you brief Sana before you go?

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Absolutely — I'll write a handover and walk her through it.

keyExpressions: I've checked and nothing major is due then.
remember: Coming with the cover already thought through turns the request from a problem into a plan.

goal: End a conversation at an event without being rude.

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: This has been really interesting — I'd love to hear more about the pilot sometime.

conversation.speaker: Them
conversation.text: Any time. Are you on LinkedIn?

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: I am, I'll send you a request tonight. I should let you circulate, but it was great to meet you.

conversation.speaker: Them
conversation.text: You too. Enjoy the rest of the evening.

keyExpressions: It was great to meet you.
I'd love to continue this another time.
Enjoy the rest of the evening.
remember: 'I should let you…' politely puts the reason on you rather than on them, which is why it never sounds like a rejection.

goal: Report a lost item and describe it clearly.

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: Excuse me, I think I left my bag on the number 12 bus.

conversation.speaker: Staff
conversation.text: When was that?

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: About an hour ago, heading into town.

conversation.speaker: Staff
conversation.text: Can you describe it?

conversation.speaker: You
conversation.text: It's a black backpack with a red zip, with a laptop inside.

conversation.speaker: Staff
conversation.text: I'll take your number and call you if it's handed in.

keyExpressions: I think I left my… on/in…
Can you describe it? — It's a…
Could you call me if it turns up?
It has my name on it.
remember: Colour, size, and one distinctive detail are all that is needed — that is exactly what staff will write down.
